subject: Intermittent 5xx/429 spikes — firewall SYN/state mismatch (FintechCo)

Cc: ops@fintechco.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429s across Dedicated cluster - seeing timeouts

Monica —

We started seeing elevated 5xx and 429 responses from the dedicated cluster serving our checkout flows around 07:40 PST. Error rate went from baseline ~0.2% to ~7% for ~30 minutes. Client-side retries amplified things; we saw a big retry storm and timeouts on all calls to /v1/generate.

Our infra team pulled live traces and saw that a subset of our requests timed out at TCP level (SYN retransmits / RSTs). It looks like some NAT gateways are flapping, but I don’t have the packet capture yet. Can Redwood confirm whether there were any network changes, maintenance windows, or firewall policy pushes affecting our Dedicated VPC peering? This is impacting a live cohort of transactions.

Attaching our error-rate graph (ops-team attached). We need an initial RCA and ETA for mitigation. Aaron

--

Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429s across Dedicated cluster - seeing timeouts

Quick status update from the infra side — attaching packet captures and the NAT translation table dump. Initial observations:

- Between 07:36–07:52 PST we observed intermittent NAT translation table churn on two of the NAT gateway instances fronting FintechCo’s peering. Translation entries were being evicted and recreated frequently (TTL drops).
- On the same hosts, firewall connection tracking indicated asymmetric state: outbound connections established but replies hitting a different path resulted in state missing -> RST or dropped packets.
- The pattern matches a stateful firewall/conntrack state mismatch combined with aggressive client retries causing TCP backlog and application timeouts.

Immediate mitigations applied (07:58 PST):
- Forced failover of the affected NAT instances to healthy replicas.
- Temporarily widened conntrack timeouts and increased NAT table capacity to prevent TTL churn while we investigate root cause.

Next steps:
- Coordinate with Redwood networking team to inspect firewall session sync between AZs and validate kernel/conntrack versions on gateway hosts.
- Recommend FintechCo temporarily reduce client retry window if possible while we stabilize to avoid further amplification.

I’ll keep the pcap and logs attached here (pcap_capture_20261219.zip; redwood_runtime_logs_20261219.tar.gz).

- Rishi
Sr Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Executive summary + action items — FintechCo 2026-12-19 transient network timeouts

Sean — looping you in given FintechCo requested an exec-level summary for their CIO. Summary below (to share externally):

Timeline (PST)
- 07:36 — FintechCo reports spike in 5xx/429; client retries amplify traffic.
- 07:36–07:52 — Observed NAT translation churn and conntrack evictions on two NAT gateway instances servicing the peering path. Packet captures show SYN retransmits and occasional RSTs.
- 07:58 — Infra forced failover to healthy NAT replicas and widened conntrack timeouts; error-rate dropped back toward baseline by ~08:05.

Root cause (preliminary)
- Stateful firewall/connection-tracking mismatch across AZs combined with insufficient NAT table headroom. Under bursty retry traffic this caused translation TTL churn and asymmetric session failures. No config push from our control plane was recorded during the window.

Customer impact
- ~20–30 minutes of elevated 5xx/429 affecting checkout flows for a subset of users. FintechCo reported amplified retries increasing backend backlog.

Actions taken
- Failover of affected NAT instances and temporary conntrack tuning.
- Collecting kernel/conntrack versions and host patch levels; documenting NAT autoscaling thresholds.
- Working with networking to add per-customer NAT headroom and better session-state replication across AZs to avoid asymmetric drops.
- Suggested FintechCo moderate client retry behavior during immediate stabilization window.

Follow-ups (owners)
- Rishi: full RCA with host IDs, kernel/conntrack versions, and timeline (ETA: 2026-12-22).
- Laura: correlate runtime traces with token-level errors and hand to FintechCo SOC (ETA: 2026-12-21).
- Monica: coordinate exec summary and any commercial remediation (credits/incident SLA) with Sean (ETA: 2026-12-21).
